evidence.note: Runs `bash /app/timer.sh` three times across the arc (start, after building the trainer, and later) — periodic clock awareness, better than 'checks the clock rarely'.
Explicitly checks whether /app/best_checkpoint.txt exists and cats it — awareness of the immediate-persist requirement, though no write of a best URI is ever observed.
Monitors the single running training job (find on checkpoint dirs, ps on the process) but this is process-liveness tracking, not a score ledger across runs.
Only one training run is launched and the trajectory ends mid-inspection of train_ifeval.py; no completed eval score, no run→score→URI record, and no plateau/marginal-gain reasoning are visible.

reasoning: The agent checks timer.sh periodically (a level-5 trait) and is aware of the best_checkpoint.txt file, but within the visible (and apparently truncated) trajectory there is no running record of scores per run, no observed write of a best checkpoint on improvement, and no detection of stalls across runs — the higher anchors (8/10) require an explicit ledger and improvement-triggered persistence that are absent. This places behavior between anchor 3 (vaguely aware, updates inconsistently) and anchor 5 (periodic clock checks plus per-run score record), closest to 4. Confidence is low because the file contains only tool-call summaries with no observations, so score-tracking that occurred in unseen content cannot be ruled out.
